subject: Streaming concurrency handshake + end-to-end latency sample matrix
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Chris Park <chris@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-10-09T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + open asks from today's performance call

Chris / Aisha — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and the handful of open asks we committed to: 

- Big picture: you asked us to validate p95/p99 end-to-end latency on a representative traffic envelope (streaming and non-streaming) and compare hosted Redwood vs your current provider.
- Next steps we agreed: provide a small traffic sample from Keystone, Redwood will propose a PoC test harness and two 2-hour test windows, then run a combined steady-state + spike run.

Open asks for your team (can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?):
1) Attach a short traffic sample (CSV/JSON) showing 1 hour of representative traffic with timestamps, request size, tokens in, tokens out, and streaming vs unary calls.
2) High-level SLA targets you expect (we heard p95 ~150ms / p99 ~350ms as a goal during the call — confirm).
3) Peak concurrent streaming sessions you expect and whether sessions are long-lived (minutes) or per-request streaming.

I'll loop SE (Camila) and Ben (AE) on the PoC plan. We can provision a hosted test rig and schedule whiteboard + test-run slots for next week.

Attachments: keystone_perf_profile.csv (placeholder for your sample), redwood_poc_plan.md (draft)

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
-----
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>
To: Chris Park <chris@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-10-09T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + open asks from today's performance call

Hi Chris — following up with specific technical probes so we can size the PoC and pick the right test configuration. A few clarifying questions and the test matrix I propose: 

Questions (please answer or point me to a sample trace):
- Are your streaming interactions client-initiated server streaming (single request, streaming response) or full-duplex? Which protocol: HTTP/1.1 chunked, HTTP/2, or gRPC?
- Average tokens generated per response (mean and 90th percentile) for the calls you'd like qualified.
- Typical request QPS and typical sustained concurrency vs short spikes (numbers: baseline QPS, expected burst QPS, observed concurrency).
- Do you terminate TLS at your edge or pass through to the inference layer? Any special auth headers we need to include?
- Do you have a caching layer / KV reuse pattern that keeps long-lived KV caches per session? If so, what percentage of requests are cold-start vs hot-cache?

Proposed minimal PoC test matrix (we can expand):
- Test A (steady-state streaming): sustained 30-minute run at baseline QPS with 10% jitter. Targets: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms.
- Test B (burst + tail probe): 10m steady + 2x burst for 3 minutes, repeated 3 times. Observe tail behavior and failover.
- Test C (concurrency ramp): ramp concurrent streaming sessions from 10 -> peak (your number) over 15 minutes to look for degradation and queueing.

For the Redwood hosted run we will:
- Use warmed model instances, measure cold vs warm start separately, collect full tracing (per-request start/end, kernel timings, queue times).
- Provide end-to-end measurement (client timestamp, Redwood ingress, egress, and client receive) so we can map where latency accumulates.

Candidate PoC slots: Oct 16 (10:00–14:00 PDT) or Oct 17 (09:00–13:00 PDT). If those don't work, we can push to Oct 20–22 as Tessa suggested.

Deliverables after the run: latency histogram per test, p95/p99 numbers, token-level cost delta vs baseline, and a short runbook recommending changes (batching, concurrency caps, streaming chunk sizing).

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
-----
From: Chris Park <chris@keystonehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-10-10T09:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + open asks from today's performance call

Tessa / Camila — thanks for the clear plan. Attaching a small sample traffic export (keystone_poc_traffic_sample.json) and a perf profile CSV. Answers inline: 

- Streaming model: single request -> streaming response (chunks every 50–200ms). Protocol: HTTP/2 streaming.
- Tokens per response: mean 42, 90th pct 120, max observed 320.
- Baseline QPS: 18 req/s (avg), typical sustained concurrency ~40 long-lived streaming sessions, peak bursts we see ~120 concurrent sessions for ~3–5 minutes during morning syncs.
- TLS: terminated at our edge LB; we will provide a test cert for the PoC.
- Cache pattern: roughly 85% hot (KV hits), 15% cold (new sessions). Cold starts add ~60–80ms on average.
- Current provider numbers (end-to-end measured from our client): p95 ~260ms, p99 ~620ms (these are noisy during spikes).

Files attached: keystone_perf_profile.csv, keystone_poc_traffic_sample.json

We can make Oct 20–22 work for the PoC. Please confirm what you need from our infra team (test cert, test API key, static IP allowlist?).

Thanks — Chris
Chris Park
Head of Infrastructure, Keystone Health
-----
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.inference>
To: Chris Park <chris@keystonehealth.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: 2025-10-11T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + open asks from today's performance call

Chris — perfect, this is exactly what we need. Confirming next steps and what Redwood will deliver before the PoC: 

1) Redwood asks from Keystone infra team: test API key and a short-lived TLS cert + IP allowlist entries for our test runner. If you prefer, we can run through your staging NAT and Kefir (your staging LB) — either is fine.
2) Redwood will produce a concrete PoC playbook (redwood_poc_plan.md) and a 3-test schedule aligned to your traffic sample.
3) We will run the hosted Redwood test first (warmed instances) and capture end-to-end traces, then run an optional test against your current provider if you want us to orchestrate it.

Proposed PoC window: Oct 20 (09:00–13:00 PDT) & Oct 21 (09:00–12:00 PDT) — please confirm.

I attached the draft PoC plan and included the HubSpot deal link here for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/48321.

If Oct 20 works we'll send calendar invites and a short pre-run checklist for your infra team (cert/key, allowlist, and verification endpoints).

Thanks — Tessa
